children: August's existing home sales report showed sales fell 2% from the prior month, falling inside of a range of Journal historical forecasts for the indicator.
The National Association of Realtors said the annual sales rate fell to 3.98 million, inside a range of Journal historical forecasts for the indicator.

For select economic indicators, including the existing home sales report, Dow Jones Newswires measures whether a reported statistic falls outside a historical range of proprietary WSJ forecasting, and if so, by how much. Those forecast ranges are based on an archive of surveys of economists the Journal has conducted over the past decade.

The gauge provides a way to measure the relative volatility of any one particular indicator, compared not just to a contemporary forecast in the days ahead of an indicator's release, but also compared to its track record surprising forecasters over time.

In the case of August existing home sales, the range of WSJ forecasts relative to the actual reported number over that 10-year period was between -1.5 percentage points and +2.1 percentage points. The month-on-month change came 0.2 percentage points higher than the 2.2% decline expected in forecasts, inside that range.

For the annual sales rate, the historical range was -80,000 to +90,000 home sales, compared to the forecast, while Thursday's number, 3.98 million, was 10,000 higher than economists' expectations, falling inside that range.
The ranges are made up of the median of historical forecasts that came in lower than the reported number and the median of forecasts that came in higher.
